focus: What Claude Code does when you ask for your first Brutalist project: reads the ai-explainer skill, drafts a beat sheet, generates Kokoro am_onyx narration, renders scenes, compiles a review cut, stops for you to judge.

16:9 vs 9:16 format discipline is important for the fellows long, but not the high-level answer to 'what does the skill do'.

cut_first_review: Story arc: B00 (Liam introduces one-ask-one-plan) -> B01 (BLUF: your first project is a claim, not a demo) -> B03 (a concrete first ask, verbatim, with the hard stop at the review cut) -> B04 (seven concrete things Claude Code does before you see a frame) -> B05 (review-cut.mp4 is a local receipt, not a published master; human review is a separate step) -> B10 (your turn: paste-ready prompt, good vs bad ask) -> B11 (Liam sign-off). Every transition already exists in the source narration (B00 'clock'->B01 'frame'; B01 'method'->B03 'first ask, verbatim'; B03 'hard stop at review cut'->B04 'seven concrete things before you see a frame'; B04 'stops'->B05 'output is a review cut'; B05 'you judge it'->B10 'your turn'; B10 'good vs bad ask'->B11 title restate).
